layers.evidence: telegram.gleam:27-36 — InboundMessage has exactly six fields: update_id, message_id, chat_id, from_user, text, timestamp_ms. There is no photo, document, audio, voice, video, sticker, animation, caption, mime_type, file_size or file_id field. A Telegram media update therefore has no representable shape in UOS; its media payload cannot be parsed because there is nowhere to put it.
layers.falsifier: Add a media field to InboundMessage and the Gleam compiler will name every construction site that must change. Today there are none to change.

layers.evidence: The only occurrence of file_id in the entire Telegram surface is telegram_simulator.gleam:84, '_file_id: String,' — a parameter of simulate_photo_upload. The leading underscore is Gleam's unused-binding marker: the value is discarded. telegram_simulator.gleam:86-93 constructs InboundMessage with text: caption and never references it. simulate_voice_memo likewise discards _duration_s (line 67) and takes the transcription as the speech_text argument, so no transcription is produced.
layers.falsifier: Remove the underscore from _file_id and the compiler reports an unused variable, proving no read path exists.

layers.evidence: SW-1 and SW-2 find zero getFile call and zero Telegram-sense file_path anywhere in UOS source. tools/telegram_client.ml (879 lines, the only module that actually speaks the Bot API) implements getUpdates at :312/:319, answerCallbackQuery at :388, deleteMessage at :365, sendChatAction at :375 and setMessageReaction at :377 — and no file method. The single media-shaped string in that file is a --help line at :742 listing 'upload_photo' as an example chat action.
layers.falsifier: grep for getFile across apps, tools and engines excluding build/: zero.

layers.evidence: Zero sendPhoto, sendDocument, sendAudio, sendVoice, sendVideo or sendMediaGroup in UOS source (SW-2). Zero MIME multipart encoder. telegram_client.ml's telegram_call marshals `Assoc JSON only, which cannot carry a file upload.
layers.falsifier: SW-2 restricted to non-build paths returns 7 hits, none of them a media send.

layers.evidence: Two functions accept bytes. telegram_simulator.gleam:97-115 simulate_acoustic_fft(sample_bytes: BitArray) computes bit_array.byte_size and branches only on size > 0, returning hardcoded AcousticSpectrum(1240, 14, 42.5, True) or all-zeros. It performs no transform of any kind. telegram_simulator.gleam:118-123 simulate_vision_inspection(image_bytes, target_bay) discards the bytes outright — 'let _ = bit_array.byte_size(image_bytes)' — and switches on target_bay. Both are called ONLY from apps/cepaf_gleam/test/telegram_simulator_test.gleam:170,174,182,188. There are zero production callers.
layers.falsifier: grep simulate_acoustic_fft|simulate_vision_inspection across src and test: 2 definitions in src, 4 call sites all in test, 0 call sites in src.

layers.evidence: No media blob store, no retention policy, no size accounting. cognitive_worker.gleam:2659-2660 writes var/telegram/evaluations/*.json — model evaluation records, not media bytes, and reached by no media path.
layers.falsifier: No field in any Telegram type holds a BitArray outside the two test-only simulator functions.

layers.evidence: Media-referencing commands are routed and do produce replies, but each reply is a fixed string. telegram_creative.gleam:86-110 handle_acoustic takes the first positional arg as an opaque label (default 'audio-exhaust-sample') and returns text asserting 'DSP Kernel: Native ZigVM 1024-point Fourier FFT Spectrogram', 'Harmonic Peak: 1,240 Hz with 14 Hz modulation flutter', 'Fault: Ball-bearing race pitting on Exhaust Fan #2 (Confidence: 94.2%)' and 'Projected RUL: 72 +/- 6 hours'. No FFT runs; no ZigVM call occurs; the AcousticProfile at :93-99 is a literal constructor. telegram_creative.gleam:55-74 handle_rack_cv (default 'photo-chassis-01') asserts 'processed by MAX/Mojo ViT model', 'Chassis Detected: 2U 24-Bay NVMe Storage Enclosure', 'Blinking Amber LED isolated on Bay 3'. telegram_collab.gleam:80-91 handle_whiteboard (default 'photo-whiteboard-session') asserts 'processed via MAX/Mojo ViT' and 'Extracted Topology: 4-State Finite State Machine' with states Idle, QuorumPending, Draining, Isolated. No MAX, Mojo or ViT invocation exists on any of these paths.
layers.hazard: This is STPA loss L-1, false conformance, at the operator-facing boundary: an operator reading 'Confidence: 94.2%' and 'Projected RUL: 72 +/- 6 hours' about a physical bearing receives a fabricated measurement presented as a diagnostic result. The failure is not a missing feature; it is a truthful-output violation (constitutional axiom Psi-5, ground-truth observed data over model assertion).

reusable_adapters.principle: Nothing in the media design needs new identity, idempotency, authorisation or ledger machinery. All four already exist and were independently verified in this review sequence. Media must enter through them, not beside them.

The root cause was mine: I grep'd for the words dedup and idempot, and zero dedup markers does not mean no idempotency. The mechanism is there and it is what media should reuse.
reuse.media_binding: A media unit of work is keyed by (update_id, message_id, file_unique_id). file_unique_id, not file_id, because Telegram documents file_id as not stable across bots while file_unique_id is stable and cannot be used to download — which is exactly the right property for a dedup key.

reuse.existing_mechanism: classify_directive at :117-147 is argument-level, not identity-level: it fixes tool names for /doctor and /plan, allowlists /tool to query_doctor|query_saplan and returns DeniedMutation otherwise, and returns explicit DeniedMutation for /approval, /andon, /resuscitate, /chaos, /rotate_keys, /repro, /merge and /zigvm.
reuse.correction_recorded: I earlier described this guard as 'identity only'. Root corrected that; the correction stands and is the reason the guard is the right place for the media deny list.
reuse.known_gap: The only canonical caller is telegram_delivery_ledger.gleam:138. Whether the guard is wired into the S1 dispatch path that telegram.gleam:245-254 uses remains UNKNOWN to me (see unresolved U-2). If it is not, a deny added here has no effect on those arms, and T0 must fix the wiring before relying on it.

reuse.reuse_for: Every media decode, transcode and inspection step.
reuse.rationale: Media decoding is the classic untrusted-parser attack surface. A bounded, timeout-enforced, reaped subprocess is the admitted UOS pattern for exactly this, and canonical policy section 5.5 requires blocking work to sit in a supervised isolated daemon rather than a NIF. No media bytes should ever be decoded inside the BEAM or inside a NIF.
reuse.bound: This review itself used the wrapper under a 25000 ms bound; media steps need far tighter bounds (see bounds table).

reuse.rationale: It already emits status UNOBSERVED, backend NOT_IMPLEMENTED and observed_in_query false. Generalise this record rather than invent a new one.

reuse.reuse_for: The Bot API transport seam, if and only if it is the surviving transport.
reuse.existing_mechanism: telegram_call with `Assoc JSON payloads; getUpdates at :312/:319; offset persisted via set_db_preference "telegram_poll_offset" at :546; sendChatAction at :375.
reuse.correction_recorded: I earlier claimed the poller and callbacks were ABSENT. That was a path-scope error: I searched src/cepaf_gleam and this file is under tools/. Retracted.
reuse.media_limit: telegram_call cannot carry an upload: a JSON `Assoc body cannot express multipart/form-data. A media send therefore needs a new, separate upload path and must not be bolted onto telegram_call.
reuse.unresolved: Whether this binary runs as a supervised service in any UOS deployment is UNKNOWN to me (U-1).

items.title: Make the eleven media arms observably unsupported, and deny the biometric arm
items.why_first: Until this lands, every later improvement sits behind an operator-facing surface that fabricates diagnostics. Building transport first would make the fabrication harder to see, not easier.
items.change: For each of the eleven arms, replace the fabricated findings block with the query_voice_status shape: a typed MediaUnsupported record carrying capability name, backend NOT_IMPLEMENTED, observed false, and the reason. Keep the command routed and keep its help text, but strip every asserted measurement — the 94.2% confidence, the 72 +/- 6 hour RUL, the detected chassis model, the extracted FSM states, the sub-120 ms pipeline latency. Separately, add /voice-roll-call to the guard's explicit DeniedMutation list at classify_directive, because an unauthenticated path offering to authenticate a constitutional vote must fail closed rather than reply politely.
items.non_goal: Do not delete the commands. Their existence is not the defect; their fabricated output is.
items.size: Five files, no new types beyond one record, no transport.

items.title: Typed media descriptor on the inbound boundary
items.change: Extend InboundMessage with an optional media field of a new sum type MediaRef, carrying kind (Photo | Document | Audio | Voice | Video | Sticker | Animation | Unsupported(String)), file_unique_id, file_id, declared_size_bytes, declared_mime, declared_duration_s and caption. Every field is what the sender declared and must be named as declared, never trusted. Parsing is total: an unrecognised media kind becomes Unsupported(raw_kind) and is never silently dropped and never treated as text.
law_obligations: A media update with an unknown kind parses to Unsupported and is reported, not discarded.
A media update with no caption does not become an empty-text command.
declared_mime is never used to choose a decoder (see sniffing rule in safety).

items.title: Bounded download adapter
items.change: A getFile -> file_path -> download path, executed through development.bounded, enforcing the bounds table before a single byte is fetched: reject on declared_size_bytes over the per-kind cap without issuing the request, then enforce the same cap again on the actual stream and abort mid-transfer when exceeded, because the declared size is attacker-controlled.
items.critical_detail: The download URL is https://api.telegram.org/file/bot<TOKEN>/<file_path> — the bot token is in the URL path. See credential_secrecy; this single fact drives three of the five secrecy rules.

items.title: Bounded content inspection, replacing the degenerate simulators
items.change: Either wire real decode behind a bounded daemon, or keep the simulators and rename them so they cannot be mistaken for measurement. simulate_acoustic_fft must not keep a name claiming an FFT while branching on byte_size > 0; simulate_vision_inspection must not keep a name claiming inspection while discarding its bytes. If real analysis is wanted, MAX/Mojo is the admitted tier (canonical policy 5.1 item 5) and Python stays confined to services/inference/max.
law_obligations: A function whose name asserts a transform either performs it or is renamed. Pinned by a test that feeds two different non-empty byte strings and requires different outputs from anything named *_fft.

items.title: Bounded media storage with explicit retention
items.change: Content-addressed store keyed by sha256 of the fetched bytes, with a declared retention horizon, a total-bytes ceiling, and fail-closed refusal when the ceiling is reached. Never store under a sender-supplied name.

items.title: Upload path, only if a use case survives review
items.change: A separate multipart/form-data sender, not an extension of telegram_call. Deliberately last: no reviewed UOS use case currently requires the bot to send media, and an unused upload path is an attack surface with no benefit.

bounds.principle: Every bound is enforced twice where the sender controls the input: once on the declared value before any work, and once on the observed value during the work. A single check on a declared value is not a bound.

size_caps_bytes.note: These are UOS policy caps, chosen to sit at or below Telegram's own download ceiling so the cap is always ours and never inherited. The exact Bot API download limit is an external fact I did not verify in this read-only task (U-4); if the official limit is lower than a cap above, the lower value wins.

bounds.type_allowlist_rule: Allowlist by magic-byte sniff of the fetched prefix, never by declared_mime and never by file extension. A declared image/png that sniffs as something else is rejected and reported as a mismatch, which is itself a signal worth recording.

identity: A media unit's identity is (update_id, message_id, file_unique_id). file_unique_id is the dedup key because it is stable and is not usable for download; file_id is carried for the fetch only and is not an identity.
Media identity flows through the existing ledger's make_request_id and same_identity, so a redelivered update cannot cause a second download.
A media unit below the ledger watermark is not re-fetched. Reuse the :175 offset-regression refusal; do not add a second watermark.
credential_secrecy: The Telegram file download URL embeds the bot token in its path. Therefore: a media URL is a credential, and the existing redaction rules that cover tokens must be extended to cover any string matching /file/bot<...>/.

A media URL is never logged, never put in a telemetry span, never written to the ledger, never included in an error message, and never surfaced to an operator. Store file_path and reconstruct the URL at the moment of the request.
Downloads carry the token only in the URL path to api.telegram.org and nowhere else; no media URL is ever handed to a subprocess as an argv element, because argv is world-readable in /proc.
The bounded inspection subprocess receives a local file descriptor or path, never a URL and never the token.

EXISTING DEFECT, carried forward from my 20261011-1302 surface plan as B3 and still unrepaired: gateway/telegram.gleam:120 places #("token", json.string(state.bot_token)) inside MCP-over-Zenoh params, which publishes the bot token onto the mesh. Media work must not build on that path until B3 is fixed, because a media design that assumes token confidentiality while B3 stands is designing against a false premise.
untrusted_content_no_execution: Fetched bytes are data. They are never executed, never eval'd, never passed to a shell, and never used to construct a command line.

No decoder runs in the BEAM or in a NIF. Decoding runs in a bounded, reaped subprocess so that a malicious file crashes a sandbox rather than the supervisor. This follows canonical policy 5.1 item 4 (native kernels are short, deterministic and non-blocking) and the Mirage ephemeral-sandbox invariant.
Sender-supplied strings are never used as filesystem paths. Storage names are derived from the content sha256 only. A caption containing ../ or a NUL must not be able to name a file.

A caption or media label echoed into a reply is escaped for the Markdown parse mode in use. This is an EXISTING LIVE DEFECT, not a hypothetical: telegram_creative.gleam:70-71 and :103-104, and telegram_collab.gleam:87-88, interpolate the sender's raw argument directly between Markdown emphasis markers. A caption containing backtick or asterisk characters can therefore break out of the intended formatting today, before any media feature is added.
The existing Hermes zero-trust interceptor already traps embedded NUL bytes (code -2) and raw SQL (code -3) on MCP dispatch. Media metadata must traverse that interceptor rather than a parallel path.
consent_and_config: Media ingestion is OFF by default. It is enabled per chat, not globally, and the enablement is configuration, not a runtime command, so no operator can turn it on from a chat message.

A media unit from a chat without consent is answered with the observable-unsupported record and is never downloaded. Refusing before fetching is the whole point: fetching first and discarding later has already copied the bytes.

Biometric capability is a separate and stricter class. /voice-roll-call offers voice biometric authentication of constitutional votes; no voice sample may ever be used as an authentication factor without an explicit, separately recorded authorisation, and until then the arm is denied at the guard rather than served.
Retention is declared and enforced, and a stored media unit is deletable on request.

shape.observed: bool, false unless this response reflects a fresh observation
shape.bound_exceeded: optional { bound: string, declared: int, cap: int }

observable_unsupported_states.rule: Every state above is reported. None of them is ever rendered as a plausible-looking result. BOUND_EXCEEDED in particular must say which bound and what the numbers were, so an operator can tell a policy refusal from a failure.
observable_unsupported_states.template: cognitive_worker.gleam:2395-2397 query_voice_status is the existing instance of this shape and should be the literal template.

positive.test: Each of the eleven media arms returns a MediaUnsupported record with backend NOT_IMPLEMENTED and observed false.
positive.oracle: Exact-string assertion per arm, so a future fabricated-findings regression fails the suite.

positive.test: No media arm's reply contains a numeric confidence, a remaining-useful-life figure, a detected hardware model, or an extracted state list.
positive.oracle: Regex refusal over the eleven replies: this is the law that pins the defect this task found.

positive.test: A photo update parses to MediaRef(Photo, ...) preserving file_unique_id and declared_size_bytes.
An update with an unrecognised media kind parses to Unsupported(raw_kind) and is reported.
A media unit within every bound downloads once and stores once; a redelivery of the same update downloads zero additional times.
positive.oracle: Existing ledger same_identity at :179-186; download counter must read 1 after two ingests.

positive.test: Two different senders uploading identical bytes produce one stored object.

negative.test: declared_size_bytes above the per-kind cap yields BOUND_EXCEEDED and issues NO network request.
negative.oracle: Request counter must be zero, not merely the result rejected.

negative.test: A stream that declares a size under the cap but actually exceeds it is aborted mid-transfer.
negative.oracle: This is the mutant that kills a single-check implementation: a design that trusts the declared size passes N-1 and fails N-2.

negative.test: A declared image/png whose fetched prefix sniffs as something else is rejected as a mismatch and the mismatch is recorded.
negative.oracle: Magic-byte oracle independent of the decoder.

negative.test: No log line, telemetry span, ledger row or error message anywhere contains /file/bot or the token bytes.
negative.oracle: Byte-level scan of all emitted output during the full media suite. This is the credential-secrecy falsifier and must run over emitted bytes, not over source.

negative.test: A caption containing ../, a NUL, or a shell metacharacter cannot influence the stored path or reach a command line.
negative.oracle: Store path must equal the content sha256 regardless of caption; argv capture must show no caption-derived element.

negative.test: A media label containing backtick and asterisk characters cannot alter the reply's Markdown structure.
negative.oracle: Escaping assertion. This test FAILS against today's code at telegram_creative.gleam:70-71, :103-104 and telegram_collab.gleam:87-88 — it is a regression test for a live defect, and it is expected to be red until T0 lands.

negative.test: A media unit from a chat without consent is answered DISABLED_BY_CONFIG and no fetch occurs.
/voice-roll-call returns DeniedMutation from the guard and never reaches a handler.
negative.oracle: classify_directive unit test alongside the existing /zigvm and /approval deny cases.

negative.test: Two different non-empty byte inputs to anything named with fft must produce different outputs.
negative.oracle: Kills the current simulate_acoustic_fft, which returns identical constants for every non-empty input. Expected red until T3.

recovery.test: A download aborted by deadline or bound leaves no partial object in the store and no half-written ledger row.
recovery.oracle: Store listing and ledger row count unchanged after the abort.

recovery.test: A crashed inspection subprocess is reaped, does not take down the supervisor, and the media unit ends in a reported failure state rather than a silent one.
recovery.oracle: Process-tree check plus terminal-state assertion. Reuse recover_request at ledger :614.

recovery.test: After a restart mid-media-unit, the unit is either completed once or reported failed once, never duplicated.
recovery.oracle: Existing ledger idempotency; download counter must not exceed 1 across the restart.

recovery.test: With the store at its total-bytes ceiling, a new media unit is refused with BOUND_EXCEEDED and the existing store is not evicted to make room.
recovery.oracle: Fail closed, do not silently discard retained evidence.

mutation_targets: Trust declared_size_bytes and skip the stream-side check — must be killed by N-2.
Choose the decoder from declared_mime — must be killed by N-3.
Include the download URL in an error message — must be killed by N-4.
Key the store on the caption instead of the content hash — must be killed by N-5.
Return a plausible AcousticSpectrum instead of UNSUPPORTED — must be killed by P-2.

limits: This is a source read. Nothing here is a runtime observation, and no claim in it constitutes two-key verification.

Absence claims are scoped to what the sweeps covered: apps, tools and engines, excluding build artefacts. mini_app_auth_clarification.root_text: Public static shell allowed only without operational data; sensitive APIs require initData plus allowlisted identity, and typed authority for actions.
mini_app_auth_clarification.bearing_on_my_prior_finding: This supersedes the open question in my 20261011-1302 surface plan finding B2 (mini-app auth enforced at one call site). Under the clarified rule, ui/wisp/mini_app_routes.gleam route/0 at :18-49 is admissible as a public static shell ONLY if every one of its 14 routes, and its catch-all _ -> dashboard_view() default, renders no operational data. That is a per-route obligation, not a blanket permission, and the catch-all is the specific risk: a route added later inherits dashboard_view() by default rather than failing closed.
mini_app_auth_clarification.media_consequence: A media viewer or thumbnail surface is operational data by definition. It therefore may not live on the public static shell and requires initData verification plus an allowlisted identity, and any media action requires typed authority. No media route may rely on the catch-all default.
mini_app_auth_clarification.not_asserted: I did not re-read mini_app_routes.gleam in this task and make no new claim about which of the 14 routes currently carry operational data. That audit belongs to the Mini App task, not to MEDIA_DESIGN.
